variants.headline: A company goes under
variants.sub: The colony has seen a company fail.
variants.body:
A company has gone under in {colony}. The failure is a business event, not a detailed account of its consequences for particular people. Readers considering {target} should distinguish that known outcome from unreported claims about creditors, employment or the circumstances that brought the company to this position.

We judge {target} critically. Business failure deserves more than a shrug, and the standards of stewardship should be examined rather than dismissed as irrelevant once an enterprise has gone under.

variants.headline: Business failure enters the colony's record
variants.sub: A business in the colony has gone under.
variants.body:
A business has failed in the colony. An enterprise is more than a name in a commercial register, but its failure does not by itself identify every consequence. An assessment of {target} should address stewardship without supplying a balance sheet or a story about the firm's trade.

We judge {target} critically. Business failure deserves more than a shrug, and the standards of stewardship should be examined rather than dismissed as irrelevant once an enterprise has gone under.

variants.headline: An enterprise reaches failure
variants.sub: A company has gone under in {colony}.
variants.body:
The colony's business record includes a company going under. That outcome invites questions of responsibility without answering them all. For {target}, the relevant scrutiny should remain separate from an invented cause, a presumed creditor loss or an announcement about workers that the report does not establish.

We judge {target} critically. Business failure deserves more than a shrug, and the standards of stewardship should be examined rather than dismissed as irrelevant once an enterprise has gone under.
